results.name: secondary-power-loss
results.title: MLAG secondary power loss
results.action: Resets the bridge on CHR 1 and CHR 2 over management SSH with the bridge mode of the run, picks the MLAG peer that reports mlag-state connected as secondary, and after a loss-free baseline emulates its power loss. In one step it takes the container veths behind the secondary's ether2 to ether5 down, sets the other peer's peer-link NIC link-down over QMP and pauses the secondary's guest with QMP stop, then confirms carrier loss at every neighbour. After 20 s it powers the secondary on with QMP system_reset and cont, brings the links back up, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

phases.name: Secondary off
phases.expected: Every link to the secondary loses carrier at once, as on a real power loss. The MLAG primary sees its peer port ether2 go down and keeps the shared system ID, so both traffic hosts keep their LACP partner. Each host drops its member to the secondary on carrier loss, without waiting for the LACP short timeout, and forwards over its member to the primary. Only traffic hashed to the lost member sees brief loss.

phases.name: Secondary back
phases.expected: Carrier returns while the secondary boots. Its bond members stay out of the 802.3ad bond until the MLAG system ID syncs with the primary (mlag-init-delay, default 1 min), then join under the unchanged shared system ID. The MLAG bonds client1 and client2 are edge ports and forward at once, so loss is brief or none.

results.name: primary-power-loss
results.title: MLAG primary power loss
results.action: Resets the bridge on CHR 1 and CHR 2 over management SSH with the bridge mode of the run, picks the MLAG peer that reports mlag-state connected as primary, and after a loss-free baseline emulates its power loss. In one step it takes the container veths behind the primary's ether2 to ether5 down, sets the other peer's peer-link NIC link-down over QMP and pauses the primary's guest with QMP stop, then confirms carrier loss at every neighbour. After 20 s it powers the primary on with QMP system_reset and cont, brings the links back up, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

phases.name: Primary off
phases.expected: Every link to the primary loses carrier at once, as on a real power loss. The MLAG secondary sees its peer port ether2 go down and reverts its MLAG bonds to its own LACP system ID (mlag-lacp-fallback=yes), so both traffic hosts renegotiate LACP, with brief loss. Each host drops its member to the primary on carrier loss, without waiting for the LACP short timeout. The secondary's edge MLAG bonds keep forwarding throughout.

phases.name: Primary back
phases.expected: Carrier returns while the primary boots. It keeps its bond members out of the bond until the MLAG system ID syncs (mlag-init-delay), rejoins as MLAG primary and restores the shared system ID. Both traffic hosts renegotiate LACP to the shared system ID, with brief loss.
